item.description:
Early Access

Email invites@kwk.co if you would like to join the alpha team, please provide a short description about why you are interested in using kwk.

Basic account commands

Follow on screen instructions.

kwk signin

kwk signout

Reset password

kwk reset-password

Change password (after a reset or with existing password)

kwk change-password

item.title: App Commands & Settings
item.description:
Your Environment

kwk relies on your local environment since it needs to have the appropriate runtimes installed (e.g. node js, ruby etc) to execute snippets and it needs editors to edit the snippets.

Normally you don’t need to install anything since kwk has been purposefully designed to work around your environment, that being said you may want to run some snippets in languages you don’t normally use so you’ll need to go to their website to grab the installers.

Tweaking Editors and Runtimes

For each machine you have kwk installed on you can configure the environment to behave in certain ways. e.g. For a build server you may want to edit snippets with Vim, for your work computer Webstorm and your home computer Sublime. But that’s not all! You can also specify certain file types be edited with certain editors. Explore the env file for details:

Snippet Editors

kwk edit env

>>>

kwkenv: "1"
editors:
#  Specify one app for each file type to edit.
  sh: [vim]
  go: [gogland]
  py: [vscode]
  url: [textedit]
  default: ["textedit"]
apps:
  webstorm: ["open", "-a", "webstorm", "$DIR"]
  textedit: ["open", "-e", "$FULL_NAME"]
  vscode: ["open", "-a", "Visual Studio Code", "$DIR"]
  vim: ["vi", "$FULL_NAME" ]
  emacs: ["emacs", "$FULL_NAME" ]
  nano: ["nano", "$FULL_NAME" ]
  default: ["open", "-t", "$FULL_NAME"]
  ...

Snippet Runners

kwk automatically creates configurations for Linux, Mac and Windows - however you can edit these if you need to run a non-default command for any particular file extension.

runners:
  sh: ["/bin/bash", "-c", "$SNIP"]
  url: ["open", "$SNIP"]
  url-covert: ["/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome", "--incognito", "$SNIP"]
  js: ["node", "-e", "$SNIP"] #nodejs
  py: ["python", "-c", "$SNIP"] #python
  php: ["php", "-r", "$SNIP"] #php
  scpt: ["osascript", "-e", "$SNIP"] #applescript
  applescript: ["osascript", "-e", "$SNIP"] #applescript
  rb: ["ruby", "-e", "$SNIP"] #ruby
  pl: ["perl", "-E", "$SNIP" ] #perl
...

Preferences

Preferences in kwk are local in that a default preference file is installed on the host computer which you can edit. For any new installation on kwk, whether reinstalling on the same machine or a new one, the last edited preferences will be installed.

kwk edit prefs

>>>

kwkprefs: v1
preferences:
  covert: false     # By default always open bookmarks in covert mode
  listall: true     # List all pouches in the root including locked
  debug: false      # Print detailed command output
  regulateupdates: true # When false will get updates as soon as they are available
  slimlines: 3      # When listing the number of snippet lines to show
  expandedlines: 15 # When expanding the number of snippet lines to show
  alwaysexpandlists: false # Always expand lines when listing
  ...

On screen help

kwk help [<command>]

Force update kwk and check version

kwk update

kwk version

item.title: Creating Apps
item.description:
Embedding Snippets

kwk ‘run’ commands can be embedded in snippets and so this opens up a whole world of opportunity to create interesting apps. Snippet references can also be dynamically passed to apps e.g./richard/apps/countdown.sh 3 'kwk tmap' will countdown and run tmap after 3 seconds.

Caveats: 1. Apps only allow 3 levels. 2. When referencing a snippet it should be an absolute name e.g. kwk run /richard/examples/hello.js. 3. Apps should have the shell .sh extension, although it is of course possible to invoke the shell from your favorite programming language. 4. There are several restrictions in .sh files e.g. you can’t use the ‘rm’ command. 5. .sh file are run in pseudo-safe mode but you can use ‘eval’ to dynamically run other kwk commands (see /kwk/apps/countdown.sh )

item.title: FAQ
item.description:
Is this free software?

Yes kwk is free for basic accounts and will always be. We will need to introduce paid accounts to help pay for hosting and development.

Where are my snippets stored?

They are replicated in near real-time in three secure data centers around the world. Edited snippets may still be in your kwk local cache, to remove this run rm -fr ~/.kwk (You will need to sign-in again).

What security do you have in place?

  • SHA256 checksums are used for all snippets and are validated prior to executing snippets and when viewing snippets.
  • Our server always chooses the transport cipher so we can upgrade it at any time. TLS 1.2 is always used.
  • With our auto-update feature you will have the latest version of kwk.
  • End-to-end encryption is coming soon.
  • Other user’s snippets cannot be run (except for /kwk/… ), you first need to clone them.
  • sudo still applies when you run snippets.

Where is the auto completion for commands?

There is none, we may add this in future but for the time being we felt it was better to focus on using intuitive commands and minimizing keystrokes.

HINT: Another cool way to save time is that many commands don’t need a specific order kwk r hello and kwk hello r are equivalent. Meaning you don’t have to back track your cursor after hitting the up arrow.

When will you have Windows support?

Soon, we do have some work already done and it is high priority. We also currently don’t support running dotnet core scripts since it has very specific folder structure requirements to compile and run.

The colors don’t look great on my terminal?

That’s not good at all! Please be a sport and log an issue.

Note: The current theme is designed for dark terminals with 256 colors.

My script is showing an error when running but the code is valid?

Scripts can only run if the correct runtime is installed! Please ensure the version of the runtime is correct too.

Can I Contribute?

We are working at making parts of the CLI open source, until then please contribute on the issue log or posting to our Twitter account.

item.title: Finding Snippets
item.description:
Saving Keystrokes

kwk has been designed specifically to save keystrokes. That’s why when typing snippet names we often try to guess which snippet you intended to use.

# Whew!
kwk view /cjones/apps/hello.js

# Better
kwk view hello.js

# Even Better
kwk view hello

# Best!
kwk hello

# Use Suggest if you can't remember the name
kwk hel


# kwk [view] [/<username>/][pouch/]<name>[.<ext>]

Note: The view command is optional. You can configure the default command for different file extensions by typing kwk edit env

Canonical Snippet names

“If it ends with a slash, it’s a directory. If not, it’s a file.” Dave Sherohman

The kwk version is: “If it ends with a slash, it’s a username or pouch. If not, it’s a snippet.”

Listing made easy

No need to keep typing ‘ls’ to list things, we actually removed that after realising how many times we typed it, so now you can list all your pouches or snippets with zero or one words, either kwk or kwk <pouch name> is enough.

Show your Homepage

Includes your pouches and unsorted snippets:

kwk

Look inside a Pouch

kwk apps

# kwk <pouch name>

Searching

kwk find worl

# kwk find [-g] <term>
# -g/--global = search everybody's public snippets.

Expanding Lists

To show more details in list, number of lines to expand can be changed by calling kwk edit prefs.

kwk expand apps

# kwk expand [<pouch name>]

Suggesting

kwk hell #RETURN
> hello.js|

Enchilada

Only use this if you really need to list all your snippets. Might be slower and lots of screen use.

kwk enchilada

Special lists

To list snippets that have been run recently:

kwk @today
kwk @week
kwk @month
kwk @old

Community

If you use a forward slash / in front of anything kwk will interpret it as a Username, thus you can browse other peoples public snippets.

kwk /alice/hawaii-trip
# Lists alice's hawaii pouch

kwk /alice/hawaii-trip/budget.txt
# Shows the details of the vacation budget

kwk /alice/hawaii-trip/hibiscus.url
# Opens the url for Hibiscus hotel

kwk run /alice/hawaii-trip/local-news.py
# Runs alice's news feed for Hawaii

# kwk /<username/[pouch name]/[snippet name]

Popular Snippets

Show Alice’s most recently used snippets

kwk /alice pop

# kwk [/<username>] popular|pop

Sharing Snippets

At the moment snippets are only shared by email.

kwk share hello.js alice

# kwk share <name>.<ext> <email>

Stale Snippets

To help you clean up use this command to show snippets which haven’t been used much or recently.

kwk stale

item.description:
Install

npm install -g kwkcli

# then

kwk signup

or if you prefer to install without npm:

curl  https://s3.amazonaws.com/kwk-cli/latest/bin/kwk-linux-amd64.tar.gz -o

// unzip

Hello world

kwk new "echo 'Hello, world!'" hello.sh

# Creates a snippet

kwk run hello

# Executes it and prints: Hello, world!

item.title: Organise with Pouches
item.description:
Stopping the mess

Pouches make categorizing snippets easy and provide a way to make a group of snippets private. Pouches have at most 24 snippets. Its important to note that a pouch is different from a folder in that snippet names still need to be unique in your entire snippet collection, with folders you can have files with the same name in different folders - not so in kwk. This decision allows us to:

  1. Reduce entropy but avoiding duplicate code and other types of snippets to accumulate.
  2. Use fewer keystrokes to address a snippet, thus even though we use pouch in an absolute path e.g. /richard/samples/hello.js - ‘samples’ is not usually used for addressing purposes, but rather cognitive categorization.*

As with snippets pouch names are all lower case * Pouch names are actually required when moving snippets - [might need to revisit this]

Create a pouch

kwk mkdir big-project
# kwk mkdir <pouch name>

View a pouch

kwk big-project
# kwk <pouch name>

Delete a pouch

kwk rm <pouch name>

Make a pouch private

kwk lock <pouch name>

Make a pouch public

kwk unlock <pouch name>

Rename a pouch

kwk mv <pouch name> <new pouch name>

Delete a pouch

kwk rm <pouch name>

item.title: Snippets
item.description:
Store anything

Snippets are often thought of as code but kwk can be used to store any small piece of information provided its no longer than 2000 *normal characters (about 100 lines), just pick a file extension which is suitable e.g. .json for some JSON or .rb for a ruby file.

URLs are well suited to be stored as snippets, in fact we have some great features for URLs including running with covert mode, meta data previews, auto url detection and by default all you need to do to open a url is type kwk my-bookmark.

** Use ‘.url’ as an extension for URLs
* Normal characters being UTF-8 non-combined characters e.g. é can be 2 characters.

Creating Snippets

A snippet is just a UTF-8 string so creating one is easy with the new or edit command:

kwk new "console.log('hello');" hello.js

# kwk new [snippet] [<name>[.<ext>]]

Note: If you add a file extension to the name the order of arguments above does not matter. Also you don’t need to provide an extension it will be given a .txt extension by default and if no name is given a random animal name will be used.

Snippet names are lowercase (they will be lowered automatically)

Create and edit in one step:

kwk edit get-weather.py

# kwk edit <name>.[<ext>]

Create a snippet from a local file:

cat ./list-open-ports.sh | kwk new open-ports.sh

# cat <file> | kwk new [<name>.<ext>]

Multi-line create with a here-doc:

kwk new <name>.<ext> <<eof
> package main
> 
> import "fmt"
> 
> func main() {
> 	fmt.Println("Hello, world")
> }
> eof

Newbie Tip:

Heredocs are really easy to use. Just type: ‘<<’ followed by any string you like to use as a terminator (in the example above it is ‘eof’). Type or paste in multiple lines after this and then finish up by typing the terminator ‘eof’ again.

Running Snippets

By default most snippets will execute only when you use the run command - the exception is web bookmarks which will run immediately. To modify which extensions need the run command edit the prefs file: kwk edit prefs.

kwk run killPort3000

# kwk [run|r] <name>[<.ext>] [args...]

Note: that in most cases bash arguments will resolve starting from $0 instead of $1 since the env.yml file uses the -c option to run snippets. The reason can be found in the bash manual:

“If arguments remain after option processing, and neither the -c nor the -s option has been supplied, the first argument is assumed to be the name of a file containing shell commands.”

Viewing Snippets

kwk hello.js
# or
kwk view hello.js

# kwk [view] <name>[.ext]

Get the raw snippet

kwk raw hello.js

# kwk raw|cat <name>[.ext]

Editing Snippets

For each machine you use kwk on you can change which editors are used for which file extensions. Use kwk edit env to change the mappings and add new editors.

kwk edit hello.js

# kwk edit <name>[.ext]

Note: When editing a snippet, kwk will watch for changes to a temporary file on the local disk, if your editor has auto-save enabled you may need to disable it or type kwk edit <name>[.<ext>] in the cli again after you’ve finished your changes so that your changes are actually saved, we are working on a more elegant fix for this.

Patching

For the most part you would use the edit command, however, patch can be useful if you want to update a snippet programatically, such as setting a version number.

kwk patch build.json "^(\d+\.)?(\d+\.)?(\*|\d+)$" "2.3.10"

# kwk patch <name>[.ext] <regex> <replacement>

Descriptions

If you are like most dev’s then remembering what a snippet does can be difficult, add a short description for list views to be more helpful.

kwk describe hello.js "A script which says hello"

# kwk describe <name>[.ext] <description>

Cloning Snippets

kwk clone /rjarmstrong/pretty-json.go slick-json.go

# kwk clone [username/][pouch/]<name>[.ext] [new name][.<ext>]

Tagging

kwk tag hello.js javascript hello-world sample

# kwk tag <name>[.ext] tag ...
# kwk untag <name>[.ext] tag ...

Moving Snippets

You can move multiple snippets between pouches provided the full relative path is given (except snippets in the root pouch can be referenced by name alone).
> Note: if the target pouch does not exist then you may end up renaming the file just like on unix systems.

kwk mv hello.js hello.go hello

# Moves snippets from the root to pouch 'hello'


kwk mv playground/hello.rs playground/hello.php hello

# Moves snippets from pouch 'playground' to 'hello'

# kwk mv <pouch>/<name>.<ext> ... <new pouch>

Renaming Snippets

kwk mv hello.js hello-world

# kwk mv <name>[.<ext>] <newname>[.<ext>]

Note: If you don’t provide an extension for the new name its possible that you may move the snippet into a pouch if one exists with that same name.

Deleting Snippets

kwk rm hello.js hello.go

# kwk rm <name>.<ext> ...

Flags

-y --auto-yes     Automatically enter 'yes' for prompts.  
-n --naked        When listing don't add styles   
-c --covert       When running a url, open it in covert mode  
-d --debug        Print output of debug  
-a --all          List all pouches including private  
-g --global       When searching include other peoples snippets
